review_scope: Independent source and mathematical reading of finite randomization claim; review of finite energy and bias–variance against sources. No code changes.

randomization.locator: Section 2, Definition 1, Theorem 1 and second proof without conditioning; section 2 permutation p values
randomization.accepted: Finite full-group upper-tail rank test has rejection probability at most alpha under a finite group-invariant probability law. The main theorem derives the pointwise rank count using an orbit reindexing argument and averages using law invariance. It counts ties conservatively.
randomization.source_relation: For alpha in [0,1), order-statistic rejection T(X) > T^(ceil((1-alpha)n)) is equivalent to #{g:T(gX)>=T(X)} <= alpha*n: the number strictly below equals n minus the upper rank, and ceil(n-alpha*n)=n-floor(alpha*n). This equivalence was checked by hand but is not formalized in Lean. The paper assumes joint statistic invariance; Lean assumes the stronger invariance of the full finite data law. Lean also permits alpha >= 1 where its bound is trivial and outside the paper's stated range.
randomization.nonvacuity: Take a two-element group acting on itself by left multiplication, uniform weights 1/2, a statistic taking values 0 and 1, and alpha=1/2. The high-statistic outcome rejects and the other does not; rejection probability is 1/2. This is a hand-checked example, not a compiled witness.
randomization.finding: Current source docstring calls the rank rule equivalent without saying that equivalence to the order-statistic rule is not formalized. Qualify it. The finite_randomization_level helper explicitly assumes the pointwise count; the principal finite_group_randomization_level proves that count. No result here proves validity of a random subset or add-one sampler, or the Python correspondence.

energy.locator: Section 5.1 Theorem 22 and immediately following proof
energy.accepted: finite_energy_kernel_identity proves the finite zero-total signed-weight cancellation step. finite_energy_nonneg proves cross-minus-within raw energy equals twice the kernel quadratic form and is nonnegative for equal-mass signed weights and symmetric finite-support PSD kernels generating d.
energy.psd_assumption: KernelPSD universally quantifies over every real coefficient vector and asserts the complete kernel quadratic form is nonnegative; it is not an assumption of the theorem's energy conclusion. Symmetry is a separate explicit hypothesis. The theorem specializes PSD to p-q only after algebraically deriving the energy identity.
energy.nonvacuity: For support {1,2}, kernel identity matrix and generated ground d(i,j)=2 when i!=j and zero otherwise, p=(1,0), q=(0,1), both mass one: kernel quadratic form is 2 and raw energy is 4. This hand-checked witness has a nonzero result; it is not a compiled witness.
energy.limits: Neither PSD from negative type, RKHS embedding nor the full measure-theoretic Theorem 22 is formalized. The squared norm or MMD interpretation is mathematical context, not directly a Lean-defined RKHS object. Python and numerical refinement remain unproved.

probability.locator: Proof P5, displayed equations MSE-ref1 and MSE-ref2
probability.accepted: The finite normalized nonnegative weight model, real-valued estimate and target, mean, variance, bias and squared-error definitions match the cited identity, and Lean follows the same centering and cancellation argument. General probability spaces and Python correspondence are outside scope.
